candidates.title: An exception thrown inside hash_tree::update (or update_words / update_sparse_tree) after page hashes were stored leaves their ancestors stale for good: m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages is set only on a false return, so later updates mark those pages clean without bubbling, and every later root hash, proof and stored snapshot is wrong (verify_hash_tree still returns true)
candidates.component: Emulator core: hash tree (src/hash-tree.cpp hash_tree::update, update_dense_trees, update_words, update_sparse_tree), reached from machine::update_hash_tree/get_root_hash/get_proof, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, log producers and send_cmio_response's revert-hash check
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md: 'Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program, hash tree, log producers, collect_mcycle_root_hashes and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, ... | Honest operator')
candidates.location: src/hash-tree.cpp: hash_tree::update lines 758-771 (m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages = !update_succeeded runs only when update returns; an exception skips it); update_dirty_pages -> return_updated_dirty_pages lines 303-314 copy the new page roots into the dense trees and lines 378-397 return the cache entries BEFORE update_dense_trees runs; update_dense_trees lines 503-511 (dense_node_entries batch{&m_memory_pool}; batch.reserve(min(m_concurrency<<10,16384)) = 64 KiB at concurrency 4, 256 KiB at >=16, an upstream allocation on every update that has a dirty range); return_updated_dirty_pages lines 384-394 (an unchanged page with m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages == false is mark_clean_page_and_up and its range is not added to changed_ars). Same flaw by reading: hash_tree::update_words lines 773-895 (copies page roots into the dht at line 873, then allocates in try_push_back(changed_ars/curr_dense_node/next_dense_node) from the pool before bubbling, and never sets m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages, neither on exception nor on the update_failures>0 false return, which also skips update_sparse_tree), and update_sparse_tree lines 541-596 (leaf hashes copied before the priority-queue loop; an exception in changed.emplace past the reserve leaves inner sparse nodes stale while the leaf-sync loop then finds leaf == dense root and never re-queues them). Field doc: src/hash-tree.hpp:252-255 says the flag exists exactly for 'an interrupted update, or a failed one'. Diagnostic gap: hash_tree::verify (hash-tree.cpp ~661-735) only compares pages with their dht page nodes and the sparse leaf with the dht root, never the inner dense nodes, so it returns true on the stale tree.
candidates.description: hash_tree::update first stores new page hashes in the dense trees (update_dirty_pages), then bubbles them up (update_dense_trees) and updates the sparse tree. The code anticipates that an update can stop half way: dirty marks are cleared only on success and m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages makes the next update re-bubble ancestors of dirty pages whose hash 'did not change' (because the failed update already stored it). But the flag is assigned only after the three steps return. If any of them throws (std::bad_alloc from the pmr pool's upstream: update_dense_trees reserves a 64-256 KiB batch on every update with a dirty range, update_sparse_tree allocates its queue and mark vector), the exception propagates with the flag still false. The next update then finds every such page unchanged (cached page root == dht node), marks it clean with mark_clean_page_and_up and leaves its range out of changed_ars, so update_dense_trees never recomputes the ancestors and update_sparse_tree's leaf sync finds the (stale) dense root equal to the leaf. The root hash stays at its old value permanently (until clear_hash_tree), later writes elsewhere only fix ancestors they share, and verify_hash_tree() returns true. update_words (used by collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes per uarch cycle and per reset) has the same window and never sets the flag at all, and an interrupted update_sparse_tree loop leaves inner sparse nodes that nothing re-queues. This is a different site and a different fix from R1-O2-3 (lost context dirty marks): fixing R1-O2-3 does not fix it, and it is reached by every operation that updates the tree, not only by the interpreter.
candidates.trigger: Host allocation failure (memory limit, RLIMIT_AS, container cgroup limit, memory-capped host) during any hash-tree update of the honest operator's running process, after which the process keeps using the machine (retries, keeps a JSON-RPC machine server, stores a snapshot). The guest only influences how many pages are dirty; the fault comes from the host. Every get_root_hash/get_proof/get_node_hash, the entry and per-period updates of collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, log_step_uarch/log_reset_uarch/log_send_cmio_response, and send_cmio_response's revert-root check perform the vulnerable allocation.
candidates.reachability: No unreachable state is involved: any machine with at least one dirty page reaches update_dense_trees, which allocates its batch through std::pmr::unsynchronized_pool_resource; a block of that size is forwarded to the upstream (operator new) on every update. The error is reported to the caller (Lua error, cm_* error code, JSON-RPC error with the server keeping the machine) and nothing documents that the machine is unusable afterwards; R9 explicitly covers 'updates that fail inside a running process, which then keeps using the machine'.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: not excluded. The candidate exclusion is 'Host faults, such as a full disk, as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state (section 4)'. Here the emulator turns the fault into a wrong root hash, wrong proofs, and a stored snapshot (store after a later successful get_root_hash) that loads with the wrong root. Section 4: 'A host fault ... may stop the honest operator, but the emulator must never turn one into a wrong hash'. No snapshot from others, no untrusted caller, documented API use.
2 Role: the hash tree is listed as 'Honest operator' in the AUDIT.md table, and section 3 says 'the hash tree and its node proofs ... play this role in every deployment'.

3 High/Medium cases: none fits. The Medium case 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree ... inconsistent (R9)' does not apply because the failing operations (get_root_hash, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, log producers) are 'Computing claims' and 'Producing proofs'. No unreachable-state case applies.

4 Critical: R9 'The content hash must equal the root of the actual contents. This applies to every cached, incremental, or persisted hash, after any sequence of documented operations. It includes interrupted or failed updates, and every snapshot the emulator itself writes.' with '"Interrupted or failed updates" means updates that fail inside a running process, which then keeps using the machine.' Violated on the honest operator's path: 'violating any rule or obligation at a reachable state, or anywhere on the honest operator's path, is critical.' Completeness: 'The honest operator computes a wrong hash'.

5 Alternative reading (Low): if an allocation failure is not a covered host fault, or is impossible 'on the resources the deployment was sized for', or continuing after an API error is 'misuse of an API by its trusted caller'. Same deciding facts as for confirmed R1-O2-3; this candidate is stronger because the window is in every hash-tree update, the code already claims to handle failed updates (hash-tree.hpp:252-255), and verify_hash_tree() does not detect the damage.
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (preferred, same reading as confirmed R1-O2-3: host fault turned into a wrong hash, R9 failed update) / Low (if memory exhaustion is not a covered host fault or continuing after an error is misuse)
candidates.threat_to_goal: A validator whose host hits a memory limit once during any hash-tree update and that keeps its machine (long-running JSON-RPC machine server, retry loop) silently computes wrong root hashes, computation hashes and proofs from then on, and snapshots it stores afterwards reload with the wrong root. Its honest claim is wrong or unprovable, so a dishonest claim can win (completeness failure, section 1). The documented sanity check verify_hash_tree() reports the tree as consistent, so even a careful operator that verifies after errors (the mitigation suggested for R1-O2-3) is not protected.
candidates.evidence: Scratch dir /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARDIRTY. c1-test.sh builds inj.cpp (LD_PRELOAD operator new replacement that throws std::bad_alloc for the request of exactly FAIL_EXACT bytes while an arm file exists) and runs c1-check.lua: 64 MiB RAM machine, runtime concurrency.update_hash_tree=4, get_root_hash, 64 write_memory calls to distinct pages, arm, get_root_hash -> std::bad_alloc (the 65536-byte update_dense_trees reservation), disarm, one more write_memory, then get_root_hash vs clear_hash_tree() rebuild: cached 0x14b95ed6... rebuilt 0xb6640061..., verify_hash_tree() == true; exits 1 (deterministic over repeated runs). probe2.lua: after the failure, one get_root_hash, write, store(dir, SHARING_ALL), load: the loaded root equals the stale 0x92da00ca... while the rebuilt root is 0xe706984e.... Fault-injection sweep (nth.cpp fails the N-th allocation while armed; sweep.sh/sweep.lua) shows the same stale root when the failing allocation is the 65536-byte update_dense_trees batch inside: plain get_root_hash (N=2), collect_mcycle_root_hashes on the R1-O2-3 guest at its entry update (N=179) and its in-loop update (N=182, verify_hash_tree true; distinct from R1-O2-3's N=180 = 131072-byte context set rehash), and log_reset_uarch (N=2, N=8). Failures of update_sparse_tree's 1024-byte mark vector self-heal (N=3). collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes and log_step_uarch sweeps (first ~300/150 allocations) did not hit the update_words window. Side observation: after some injected failures the next allocation from the same std::pmr::unsynchronized_pool_resource segfaults inside libstdc++ (st=139, size 192 requests), and some failures inside Lua result conversion abort via std::terminate (st=134); those are crashes (stops), not wrong hashes.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh like R1-O2-3: build an exact-size bad_alloc injector, create a machine with concurrency.update_hash_tree fixed (so the update_dense_trees reservation size is known: (concurrency<<10)*16 bytes), dirty some pages with write_memory, arm, pcall(get_root_hash) must fail with the injected bad_alloc (else exit 2), disarm, then require get_root_hash() == root after clear_hash_tree() (exit 1 if not). Also assert that verify_hash_tree() returns false whenever the cached root differs from the rebuilt one. A fix would set m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages = true before the first dht write (and clear it only on success) in update, update_words and update_sparse_tree, or catch, set the flag, and rethrow.

candidates.title: Log producers are not atomic under a host fault: an exception while recording (log_step_uarch, log_send_cmio_response, also errors raised after the transition) leaves the machine partway through the logged transition (pc advanced without uarch_cycle, imcyclemax and revert root hash written while iflags.Y stays set) or fully advanced while reporting failure; a retry on the same machine then logs and hashes a different trajectory
candidates.component: Log producers: machine::log_step_uarch with uarch_record_state_access, machine::log_send_cmio_response with record_send_cmio_state_access, machine::log_reset_uarch (and the cm_/Lua wrappers that convert results after the operation)
candidates.role: Honest operator (log producers are listed as Honest operator in the AUDIT.md table)
candidates.location: src/uarch-record-state-access.hpp log_write_access (lines 162-185): the write functor runs, then log_written_hash / log_written_data / log_access(push_access) allocate; any bad_alloc there unwinds after the machine word was written. src/record-send-cmio-state-access.hpp log_before_write (push_access before the write) and log_write_memory_with_padding (lines 194-250: write_memory + fill_memory + update_hash_tree, then written_hash/written_data emplace and m_log.push_access(a) copying the access with up to 2 MiB of read data). src/send-cmio-response.cpp writes imcyclemax, then the revert root hash, then the rx data, then fromhost, then iflags.Y, each logged separately. src/machine.cpp log_step_uarch 2193-2216 and log_send_cmio_response 2107-2131 run verify_* after the state change and throw on any failure there (also on bad_alloc), as do the cm.cpp/clua JSON conversions of the returned log.
candidates.description: A logged transition is applied to the machine access by access, and the access log is built with heap allocations interleaved with those writes. A std::bad_alloc (or any exception) thrown by the logging code between two writes unwinds out of uarch_step / send_cmio_response and leaves the machine with only part of the transition applied, a state that no transition of the state transition function produces. Measured: log_step_uarch leaves uarch_pc advanced while uarch_cycle is not incremented; log_send_cmio_response leaves imcyclemax set (and then the revert root hash, the rx buffer and htif.fromhost written) while iflags.Y is still 1. Failures after the last write (verify_step_uarch/verify_send_cmio_response, JSON conversion) report an error although the transition was fully applied. The hash tree stays consistent with these contents, so get_root_hash returns the root of the half-applied state. A caller that retries the same API call on the same machine gets: for log_step_uarch, a step executed from the half state (with pc already advanced the next instruction is executed and the uarch trajectory diverges from the canonical one: retry root != control); for log_send_cmio_response, a log whose before-hash is the half state, which no referee accepts against the canonical before-hash, while send_cmio_response with the canonical revert hash now refuses ('revert root hash does not match'); a caller that passes the current root as revert hash (as the harness README example does) records a wrong revert root hash (R6). This is the same family as R1-O2-3's side observation (mcycle not written back after an exception) but at the log producers.
candidates.trigger: Host allocation failure during log_step_uarch / log_send_cmio_response / log_reset_uarch on a machine the process keeps using (or a retry of the call on the same machine). Larger logs (LARGE_DATA delivery logs of a 64 KiB input copy ~2x the write size after the write) raise the chance.
candidates.reachability: Any reachable state; the fault comes from the host. The PRT player (support) logs on a fresh fork it discards (prt.lua prove_state_transition), so it is not affected; whether a production node logs on its main machine is unknown, which is what decides the impact.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: arguably not excluded: 'Host faults ... as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof' and section 4 'the emulator must never turn one into a wrong hash'. The machine's own root hash after the error is the hash of a non-canonical state, and a retry produces a log/hash of a transition the STF does not define. Under the reading that only the reported error matters and a retry after an error is 'misuse of an API by its trusted caller', it is Low.
2 Role: log producers are 'Honest operator' in the AUDIT.md table (section 3: 'its log producers ... play this role in every deployment').
3 High/Medium: no listed case fits (the state is reachable; the operation is 'Producing proofs' on the honest operator's path).

4 Critical (strict reading): R4 'Input delivery with the referee parameters of its position never fails' and 'No reachable state makes a log producer fail', together with the section 4 host-fault clause; R9's definition of failed updates ('updates that fail inside a running process, which then keeps using the machine') shows the model expects a machine to remain usable after a failed call, but here the contents themselves are left at a state no execution reaches. O2's 'A stop at any other point, even partway through an instruction or an API call, can leave registers, memory and the hash tree in a combination that no execution reaches' covers only stops (crash, kill, power loss), not a failed call inside a running process.

5 Low (preferred by me): the hash tree stays consistent with the contents, the failure is reported, and the known honest-operator implementation logs on disposable forks; it violates a rule only if continuing to use a machine after a failed log call is a documented use.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (preferred: failure is loud and the state hash is consistent; needs continued use after an API error) / Critical (if continued use of the machine after a failed call is documented use, by analogy with R1-O2-3's R9 reading)
candidates.threat_to_goal: A node that logs on its main machine and retries after a host allocation failure continues from a state no transition reaches: its later uarch trajectory, claims and proofs differ from the canonical ones (wrong hash), or its delivery proof cannot verify (no proof), so the honest claim can be lost.
candidates.evidence: Scratch dir /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARDIRTY. nth.cpp (LD_PRELOAD: throw std::bad_alloc on the N-th allocation while an arm file exists). logstep.lua on the R1-O2-3 bare-metal guest at mcycle 1,000,000 with K preliminary uarch steps: for K=0, N=25..28 the failed log_step_uarch leaves uarch_cycle=0 with uarch_pc=0x600004 (control after one step: cycle 1, pc 0x600004) and a retry ends at a root different from the control's; N=20..24 leave a register written without pc/cycle (retry happens to match); N>=29 the step completed but the call failed (a retry double-steps). Same pattern at K=5. logsend.lua on bugs/harness valid-template (accepted manual yield, 60,000-byte payload, LARGE_DATA log): N=18..21 leave imcyclemax=281475044577870 (changed) with iflags.Y=1 and revert root hash unchanged; N=22..44 also the revert root hash written; N=45..48 also htif.fromhost=0xeb84 with Y=1; N>=49 fully delivered but the call failed. sweep.lua found no hash-tree staleness for log_step_uarch beyond candidate 1's window.
candidates.test_idea: With the N-th-allocation injector, for every N up to the call's allocation count, pcall(log_step_uarch) / pcall(log_send_cmio_response) on fresh machines and require that after a failure the machine's root hash equals either the before-hash (transition not applied) or the after-hash of a control run (fully applied, and then the call should not report failure); exit 1 on any third value (e.g. uarch_pc advanced with uarch_cycle unchanged, or imcyclemax changed with iflags.Y == 1). A fix: build the log entries without allocating between writes (preallocate), or apply the transition on the machine only after the log has been built, or roll back on exception.

not_covered: update_words exception window (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes) and update_sparse_tree mid-queue interruption were established by reading only; the N-th allocation sweep over the first ~300 allocations of a 3-mcycle collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes did not hit them (pool allocations are rare in steady state).

JSON-RPC server handlers (jsonrpc-remote-machine.cpp) were not exercised: I relied on R1-O2-3's finding that the server catches std::exception and keeps serving the same machine; fork_server/rebind and remote store/load paths not examined.
send_cmio_response (state_access, non-logged) was checked by reading only: it performs no allocation and no throwing call between its writes, so it looked atomic; not fault-injected.

run, run_uarch, reset_uarch, write_memory, fill_memory, write_word, replace_memory_range, store/clone/sync were read for change-then-bookkeeping ordering (mark_dirty_page_and_up is noexcept and follows each write; always-dirty shadow pages; write-TLB pages marked before slot overwrite) and found consistent; only get_root_hash, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, log_step_uarch, log_reset_uarch and log_send_cmio_response were fault-injected.

Exceptions other than std::bad_alloc (e.g. a uarch trap exception, 'uarch reached its maximum cycle', console flush errors) were reasoned about only: collect_uarch leaves DPT marks for memory and relies on always-dirty shadow pages, so its hash tree stays consistent; uarch traps from reachable states are a separate (R3/R4) question.

The libstdc++ std::pmr::unsynchronized_pool_resource segfault on the allocation that follows an upstream bad_alloc (observed, size-192 requests) and std::terminate in Lua/JSON result conversion on bad_alloc were not analysed further (crashes are stops, not wrong hashes).
Stored-directory consequences beyond one store(SHARING_ALL)+load round trip (sync, SHARING_NONE/CONFIG, persisted m_bubble_up_unchanged_pages across reload) were not tested.
verify_hash_tree() not checking inner dense nodes was noted as part of candidate 1, not audited as a separate diagnostic.
Real memory-limit triggers (RLIMIT_AS, cgroup) were not run; all faults were injected with LD_PRELOAD operator new replacements.
record_step_state_access / log_step (main-processor step log) are ZK-only and out of scope; not examined.
